processed_hadiths.english_translation: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim said: Malik said: When the imam sits on the minbar on Friday and the mu'adhdhins call the adhan, at that time buying and selling becomes disliked. If a man buys or sells at that time, that transaction is nullified. Malik disliked that women, slaves, or children - those upon whom Friday prayer is not obligatory - should buy or sell from Muslims at that time. I said to Ibn al-Qasim: Is what these people who are not obligated to attend Friday prayer buy or sell nullified according to Malik's statement? He said: Malik said: The buying and selling of those not obligated to attend Friday prayer is not nullified, and that is my opinion. I said: What if one who is obligated to attend Friday prayer buys from a child or slave? He said: The transaction is nullified. Then Malik used as evidence the case of one who buys food from a Christian or Jew, when the Christian bought it by measure and then sold it to the Muslim before the Christian or Jew measured it. I said: Is his sale invalid? He said: Yes, that is what Malik said. Then he said: When one who is obligated to attend Friday prayer buys from or sells to one who is not obligated to attend, the transaction is nullified. Malik said: The imam should not prevent the people of the markets from selling on Friday. Malik said: When the mu'adhdhin calls the adhan and the imam sits on the minbar, he prevents people from buying and selling - men, slaves, and women. Malik said: It reached me that some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that a man should abandon work on Friday as the Jews and Christians abandoned work on Saturday and Sunday. Ibn Wahb said, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, that 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz used to prevent people from selling when the call to prayer was made on Friday. Ibn Wahb said, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Ibn Shihab, he said: Calling out for selling becomes prohibited when the imam comes out on Friday. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and Zayd ibn Aslam said the same. Ibn Wahb said, from Abu al-Zinad, from his father, that he said: It is nullified. Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: It is nullified.

الَّذِينَ لَا تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْجُمُعَةَ فِي قَوْلِ مَالِكٍ ؟ قَالَ : قَالَ مَالِكٌ : لَا يُفْسَخُ شِرَاءُ مَنْ لَا تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْجُمُعَةُ ، وَلَا بَيْعُهُ وَهُوَ رَأْيِي . قُلْتُ : فَإِنْ كَانَ اشْتَرَى مَنْ تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْجُمُعَةَ مِنْ صَبِيٍّ أَوْ مَمْلُوكٍ ؟ قَالَ : فَالْبَيْعُ مَفْسُوخٌ , ثُمَّ احْتَجَّ مَالِكٌ بِالَّذِي اشْتَرَى الطَّعَامَ مِنْ نَصْرَانِيٍّ أَوْ يَهُودِيٍّ , وَقَدِ اشْتَرَاهُ النَّصْرَانِيُّ عَلَى كَيْلٍ ، فَبَاعَهُ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَكْتَالَهُ النَّصْرَانِيُّ أَوِ الْيَهُودِيُّ . قُلْتُ : فَبَيْعُهُ غَيْرُ جَائِزٍ ؟ قَالَ : نَعَمْ كَذَلِكَ قَالَ مَالِكٌ , ثُمَّ قَالَ : إِذَا اشْتَرَى أَوْ بَاعَ مَنْ تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْجُمُعَةَ مِمَّنْ لَا تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْجُمُعَةَ فَالْبَيْعُ مُنْتَقَضٌ . قَالَ : وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ : لَا يَنْبَغِي processed_hadiths.english_translation: Ibn al-Qasim said: Malik said regarding the imam who is giving the khutbah on Friday and experiences hadath in the middle of his khutbah: He should command a man to complete the khutbah and lead them in prayer. If he experiences hadath after finishing his khutbah, then likewise he should appoint a man as his substitute to lead them in Friday prayer, two rak'ahs. I said: What if he appoints a man who did not attend the khutbah? He said: It reached me from Malik or others among the people of knowledge that they disliked that anyone who did not attend the khutbah should lead them in prayer. But if he does so, I hope their prayer will suffice them. I said to Ibn al-Qasim: If an imam led people in prayer and experienced hadath, so he left and went away without appointing a substitute? He said: I did not ask Malik about this. Ibn al-Qasim said: I see that they should appoint a man to lead them in the remainder of their prayer. I said: If they prayed individually when their imam left because of his hadath and he did not appoint a substitute, does it suffice them to pray for themselves without appointing a substitute for the remainder of their prayer? He said: As for Friday prayer, it does not suffice them. As for other than Friday prayer, that suffices them, if Allah wills, because Friday prayer can only be with an imam. Malik said regarding the imam who experiences hadath on Friday while delivering the khutbah: He appoints a substitute to complete the remainder of the khutbah and lead them in prayer, and he does not complete the remainder of the khutbah after experiencing hadath. Ibn al-Qasim said regarding the imam delivering the khutbah on Friday who experiences hadath during his khutbah, or after finishing it before entering ihram, or after entering ihram: All of that is the same, and he appoints someone to complete for the people the remainder of what was upon him of the khutbah or the prayer. If he is ignorant of that or deliberately abandons it, the people appoint for themselves someone to complete that for them, and their prayer suffices. Ibn al-Qasim said: They should appoint someone who attended the khutbah - that is more beloved to me. If they appoint someone who did not attend the khutbah and he leads them in prayer, their prayer suffices them, but I do not like that they intentionally do so. Malik said regarding the imam who experiences hadath on Friday and appoints a man in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity), forgetful of his janabah or remembering it, to lead them: Friday prayer in this case and other prayers are the same. If he was forgetful and led them, their prayer is complete and they do not repeat it. If he remembered it and led them, their prayer is invalid. If he left after entering the prayer niche before doing anything of the prayer, and he appointed someone or they appointed someone who led them, their prayer is complete and they do not repeat it. Malik said regarding the imam who experiences hadath and appoints a madman in his state of madness or a drunkard in his state of drunkenness to lead Friday or other prayers: He is like one who did not appoint anyone. If he leads them, their prayer is invalid and does not suffice them. Malik said regarding the imam who experiences hadath on Friday and leaves without appointing a substitute, so a man comes forward on his own initiative while the people did not appoint him nor did their imam: That suffices them and he is like one whom the imam or those behind him appointed, and Friday prayer in this is the same as other prayers. Malik said regarding the imam who experiences hadath on Friday and appoints as substitute one who did not reach the ihram with him, when the imam had already entered ihram and those behind him, and this one entering enters ihram after entering: Their prayer is nullified and is not valid, and they are like people who enter ihram before their imam - their prayer is not valid. The prayer of this appointed substitute is also not valid for Friday prayer because he has become alone, and Friday prayer is not performed by one person alone, and they all must repeat Friday prayer. Malik said regarding one who delivered the khutbah and experienced hadath, so he appointed a substitute: He leads the people in two rak'ahs. Ibn al-Qasim said: Whoever experiences hadath on Friday while the imam is delivering the khutbah - Malik said: He leaves without permission, and that permission was only during the military campaigns of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it has not reached me that this was regarding Friday prayer.

الْإِمَامُ , وَمَنْ خَلْفَهُ فَيُحْرِمُ هَذَا الدَّاخِلُ بَعْدَمَا يَدْخُلُ : إِنَّ صَلَاتَهُمْ مُنْتَقَضَةٌ وَلَا تَجُوزُ وَهُمْ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْقَوْمِ يُحْرِمُونَ قَبْلَ إِمَامِهِمْ , فَلَا تَجُوزُ وَالْإِمَامُ يَخْطُبُ , قَالَ : قَالَ مَالِكٌ : يَنْصَرِفُ بِلَا إِذْنٍ , وَإِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ الْإِذْنُ كَانَ فِي حَرْبِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ , وَلَمْ يَبْلُغْنِي أَنَّ processed_hadiths.english_translation: Ibn al-Qasim said: It reached me from Malik that he said regarding an imam who gave the khutbah to the people, then when he finished his khutbah, a different wali (governor) appointed someone else, so he entered the mosque: He should not lead them in prayer, but rather the one who delivered the khutbah should lead them in prayer. I said to Ibn al-Qasim: What if the one who delivered the khutbah refused and the one appointed by the wali led them in prayer? He said: I see that they should repeat their prayer. He said: Malik said: If a man delivers the khutbah to the people, he has more right to lead them in prayer unless he appointed someone to lead them before he finished delivering the khutbah. Ibn al-Qasim said: If he appointed someone while he was delivering the khutbah before completing it, I see that the one he appointed should complete the khutbah, as we mentioned previously. I said: What if the one who delivered the khutbah left after he finished, before entering ihram, and another man led them in prayer without him appointing anyone? Ibn al-Qasim said: I do not like that the khateeb (one who delivered the khutbah) should do that. If he does so and leaves without appointing a substitute, then if the people appoint someone to lead them in prayer, I see that their prayer suffices them. However, I dislike that the khateeb should do what he did in deliberately abandoning leading them in prayer. If he had an excuse other than deliberate abandonment, then there is no problem in what the people did in appointing someone to lead them in prayer, and their prayer suffices them. Malik said: Regarding the man who enters while the imam is delivering the khutbah on Friday - I see that he should sit and not pray two rak'ahs. I said: Why? He said: Because they narrate that the Prophet ﷺ forbade prayer and speech when the imam delivers the khutbah. I said: What if he prayed two rak'ahs when the imam was delivering the khutbah? He said: I do not see that he should repeat them, and what he did suffices him if he prayed them. Sahnun said: The prohibition of prayer when the imam delivers the khutbah is for the one who entered the mosque and found the imam delivering the khutbah. As for one who was sitting when the imam started the khutbah, he may pray the two rak'ahs that he owes before the imam starts delivering the khutbah. He said: Malik was asked about the man who enters when the imam is delivering the khutbah and finds a space that he can only reach by stepping over people - should he step over them or sit where he is? He said: Rather, he should sit where he is and not step over people. Malik was asked about men who sit in a circle and talk while the imam is delivering the khutbah: Do you see that they should be separated? He said: Yes, they should be separated, and I dislike that. Malik disliked that a man should lie down when the imam is delivering the khutbah or lean on his hand. Malik said: If the imam prolongs the sitting between the two khutbahs, I see nothing wrong with that. I said: Can he deliver one khutbah? He said: No, there must be two khutbahs. He said: Malik said: There is no specific thing that the imam must say in the khutbah, but rather he praises Allah and mentions the Prophet ﷺ and reminds and admonishes. Malik was asked: Can the imam sit while delivering the khutbah? He said: I have not heard of that, and I have not seen anyone do it. But if illness or some excuse forced him to do so, I see nothing wrong with that. Malik was asked about the imam who delivers the khutbah in a language other than Arabic: He said: I dislike that, and I have not heard of it. Malik said: The imam should not recite Quran in the khutbah on Friday. He said: Malik disliked that a man should make tasbeeh (glorification) or dhikr when the imam is delivering the khutbah on Friday, but he did not see a problem with moving his lips without making his voice heard. Ibn al-Qasim said: I asked Malik about the man who teaches his young son when the imam is delivering the khutbah or corrects him in Quran recitation? He said: I dislike all of that. Ibn al-Qasim said: Regarding one who enters the mosque on Friday and finds the imam delivering the khutbah and another man standing praying: Malik disliked that he should wait for him to finish so he could pray with him.

processed_hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ ابْنُ الْقَاسِمِ : وَبَلَغَنِي عن مَالِكٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي إِمَامٍ خَطَبَ النَّاسَ ، فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ خُطْبَتِهِ قَدَّمَ وَالٍ سِوَاهُ فَدَخَلَ الْمَسْجِدَ ، قَالَ : لَا يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ بِالْخُطْبَةِ الْأُولَى خُطْبَةِ الْإِمَامِ الْأَوَّلِ ، وَلَكِنْ    @ 1 : 175 @    يَبْتَدِئُ لَهُمُ الْخُطْبَةَ هَذَا الْقَادِمُ . وَقَالَ ابْنُ الْقَاسِمِ فِي إِمَامٍ يُقَصِّرُ فِي بَعْضِ الْخُطْبَةِ أَوْ يَنْسَى بَعْضَهَا أَوْ يُدْهَشُ , فَيُصَلِّي بِالنَّاسِ : إِنَّهُ إِنْ خَطَبَ بِهِمْ مَا لَهُ مِنْ كَلَامِ الْخُطْبَةِ قَدْرٌ وَبَالٌ أَجْزَأَتْ عنهُمْ صَلَاتُهُمْ , وَإِنْ كَانَ إِنَّمَا هُوَ الْكَلَامُ الْخَفِيفُ مثل الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَنَحْوُهُ أَعَادُوا الْخُطْبَةَ وَالصَّلَاةَ . وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ فِي الْإِمَامِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ يَجْهَلُ ، فَيُصَلِّي قَبْلَ الْخُطْبَةِ ثُمَّ يَخْطُبُ : إِنَّهُ يُصَلِّي بِالنَّاسِ ثَانِيَةً ، وَتُجْزِئُ عنهُمُ الْخُطْبَةُ ، وَيُلْغِي مَا صَلَّى قَبْلَ الْخُطْبَةِ . قَالَ : وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ فِي خُطْبَةِ الْإِمَامِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ يَمْسِكُ بِيَدِهِ عَصًا , قَالَ مَالِكٌ : وَهُوَ مِنْ أَمْرِ النَّاسِ الْقَدِيمِ . قُلْتُ لَهُ : أَعَمُودٌ الْمِنْبَرَ يَعني مَالِكٌ أَمْ عَصَا سِوَاهُ ؟ قَالَ : لَا بَلْ عَصَا سِوَاهُ . وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ فِي إِمَامٍ يُصَلِّي يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ أَرْبَعًا عَامِدًا أَوْ جَاهِلًا وَقَدْ خَطَبَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ : إِنَّهُ يُلْغِي صَلَاتَهُ تِلْكَ ، وَيُعِيدُ الصَّلَاةَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ , وَلَا يَعْتَدُّ بِمَا صَلَّى قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ ، وَتَكْفِيهِ خُطْبَتُهُ الْأُولَى . قُلْتُ لِابْنِ الْقَاسِمِ : مَا قَوْلُ مَالِكٍ فِيمَنْ صَلَّى الظُّهْرَ فِي بَيْتِهِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ الْإِمَامُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ ؟ قَالَ : أَرَى أَنَّهُ لَا تُجْزِئُهُ صَلَاتُهُ   ، وَلَا تَجْزِيءُ أَحَدًا صَلَّى الظُّهْرَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ قَبْلَ الْإِمَامِ مِمَّنْ تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْجُمُعَةُ لِأَنَّ الظُّهْرَ لَا يَكُونُ إِلَّا لِمَنْ فَاتَتْهُ الْجُمُعَةُ , قَالَ : وَهَذَا تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْجُمُعَةُ . وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ فِي الْأَمِيرِ الْمُؤَمَّرِ عَلَى بَلَدٍ مِنَ الْبُلْدَانِ يَخْرُجُ فِي عَمَلِهِ مُسَافِرًا : أَنَّهُ إِنْ مَرَّ بِقَرْيَةٍ مِنْ قُرَاهُ تُجَمَّعُ فِي مِثْلِهَا الْجُمُعَةُ , وَكَذَلِكَ إِنْ مَرَّ بِمَدِينَةٍ مِنْ مَدَائِنِ عَمَلِهِ جَمَعَ بِهِمُ الْجُمُعَةَ , وَإِنْ جَمَعَ فِي قَرْيَةٍ لَا يُجَمِّعُ فِيهَا أَهْلُهَا لِصِغَرِهَا فَلَا يُجْزِئُهَا , وَإِنَّمَا كَانَ لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُجَمِّعَ فِي الْقُرَى الَّتِي يُجَمَّعُ فِي مِثْلِهَا إِذَا كَانَتْ فِي عَمَلِهِ وَإِنْ كَانَ مُسَافِرًا لِأَنَّهُ إِمَامُهُمْ , قَالَ : وَمَنْ صَلَّى مَعَ هَذَا الْإِمَامِ الْجُمُعَةَ فِي الْمَوْضِعِ الَّتِي لَا تَكُونُ فِيهِ جُمُعَةٌ , فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ لَهُمْ ظُهْرٌ وَيُعِيدُونَ صَلَاتَهُمْ وَلَا يُجْزِئُهُمْ مَا صَلَّوْا مَعَهُ وَيُعِيدُ الْإِمَامُ أَيْضًا , وَلَا يَعْتَدُّ بِتِلْكَ الصَّلَاةِ وَإِنْ صَلَّاهَا بِهِمْ .E160 قَالَ : وَقَالَ ابْنُ نَافِعٍ ، عن مَالِكٍ : تُجْزِئُ الْإِمَامَ . قَالَ : وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ : لَا يُصَلِّي الْعَبْدُ بِالنَّاسِ الْعِيدَ وَلَا الْجُمُعَةَ لِأَنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَا جُمُعَةَ عَلَيْهِ وَلَا عِيدَ . وَقَالَ ابْنُ الْقَاسِمِ فِي الْإِمَامِ يَخْطُبُ ، فَيَهْرُبُ النَّاسُ عنهُ ، وَلَا يَبْقَى مَعَهُ إِلَّا الْوَاحِدُ وَالِاثْنَانِ , وَمَنْ لَا عَدَدَ لَهُ مِنَ الْجَمَاعَةِ وَهُوَ فِي خُطْبَتِهِ أَوْ بَعْدَمَا فَرَغَ مِنْهَا : إِنَّهُمْ إِنْ لَمْ يَرْجِعُوا إِلَيْهِ ، فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمُ الْجُمُعَةَ صَلَّى أَرْبَعًا وَلَمْ يُصَلِّ بِهِمُ الْجُمُعَةَ , وَلَا تُجَمَّعُ الْجُمُعَةُ إِلَّا بِجَمَاعَةٍ وَإِمَامٍ   وَخُطْبَةٍ . وَقَالَ ابْنُ الْقَاسِمِ فِي الْإِمَامِ يُؤَخِّرُ الْخُرُوجَ إِلَى الْجُمُعَةِ ، وَيَأْتِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ مَا يُسْتَنْكَرُ : إِنَّهُمْ يُجَمِّعُونَ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ إِنْ قَدَرُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ , فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ صَلَّوْا فُرَادَى لِأَنْفُسِهِمُ الظُّهْرَ أَرْبَعًا ، وَيَتَنَفَّلُونَ صَلَاتَهُمْ مَعَهُ . وَقَالَ ابْنُ الْقَاسِمِ : وَأَخْبَرَنِي مَالِكُ بْنُ أَنَسٍ ، أَنَّ الْقَاسِمَ processed_hadiths.english_translation: Malik said regarding people who came to Friday prayer but missed it: Do you see that they should pray Dhuhr four rak'ahs in congregation in a mosque other than the congregational mosque? He said: No, and they should pray as individuals (not in congregation) four rak'ahs. This is because congregational prayer on Friday is only in one mosque. He said: If the imam led them in Friday prayer in the congregational mosque, then they - meaning these who missed it - should not pray in congregation in a mosque other than it. Rather, they should pray as individuals. This applies to a town that has only one Friday prayer. I said: What is your view if they prayed in congregation? Ibn al-Qasim said: I see that they should repeat their prayer individually and not in congregation, if they deliberately did so.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: There is no Friday prayer during all the days of Mina in Mina, nor on the Day of Tarwiyah in Mina, nor on the Day of 'Arafah in 'Arafah. I said to Malik: What if a man enters Mecca before Friday - should he pray Friday or Dhuhr? He said: Friday. If he fears missing the station (at 'Arafah), then Dhuhr. I said: What if he enters on Friday before the sun sets? He said: If he entered after the prayer (i.e., after Friday prayer was completed), then he should pray Dhuhr. If he entered before the prayer, then Friday. Ibn al-Qasim said: If he comes to 'Arafah on the night of 'Arafah (i.e., the night before the Day of 'Arafah), he prays there the dawn prayer and does not enter Mecca for Friday prayer. This is because he would miss the station. And Friday prayer does not exist in 'Arafah. I said: Regarding one who is at 'Arafah and the sun sets before he prays Dhuhr - what should he do? Ibn al-Qasim said: If he deliberately delayed it, he should make it up as Dhuhr. I have not asked Malik about this.
